claim: When a file was in a zip archive, the archive was downloaded and the targeted file was selectively extracted.
source: When a .mdp or .gro file was found to be in a zip archive, the latter was downloaded and the targeted .mdp or .gro file was selectively extracted from the archive.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this procedure.

claim: The same procedure was applied for a subset of .xtc files (about one per Gromacs dataset).
source: The same procedure was applied for a subset of .xtc files that consisted of about one .xtc file per Gromacs datasets.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this procedure.

claim: .mdp files were parsed to extract integrator, time step, number of steps, temperature, thermostat, and barostat.
source: Once downloaded, .mdp files were parsed to extract the following parameters: integrator, time step, number of steps, temperature, thermostat, and barostat.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly lists the extracted parameters.

claim: Values for thermostat and barostat were normalized according to Gromacs documentation.
source: Values for thermostat and barostat were normalized according to values provided by the Gromacs documentation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this normalization.

claim: For simulation time analysis, .mdp files with md or sd integrator and simulation time above 1 ns were selected to exclude minimization and equilibrating simulations.
source: For the simulation time analysis, we selected .mdp files with the md or sd integrator and with simulation time above 1 ns to exclude most minimization and equilibrating simulations.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this selection criterion.

claim: For thermostat and barostat analysis, only files with non-missing values listed in Gromacs documentation were considered.
source: For the thermostat and barostat analysis, only files with non-missing values and with values listed in the Gromacs documentation were considered.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this selection criterion.

claim: .gro files were parsed with MDAnalysis library to extract the number of particles.
source: The .gro files were parsed with the MDAnalysis library (Michaud-Agrawal et al., 2011) to extract the number of particles of the system.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this with a citation.

claim: Residue names from .gro files were compared to a manually associated list of categories.
source: Values found in the residue name column were also extracted and compared to a list of residues we manually associated to the following categories: protein, lipid, nucleic acid, glucid and water or ions (https://github.com/MDverse/mdws/blob/main/params/residue_names.yml; Poulain et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this with a citation.

claim: .xtc files were analyzed using the gmxcheck command to extract number of particles and frames.
source: The .xtc files were analyzed using the gmxcheck command (https://manual.gromacs.org/current/onlinehelp/gmx-check.html) to extract the number of particles and the number of frames.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this procedure.

claim: The MDverse data explorer web application was built in Python with the Streamlit library.
source: The MDverse data explorer web application was built in Python with the Streamlit library.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this.

claim: Data for the web application was downloaded from Zenodo.
source: Data was downloaded from Zenodo (see the Data availability statement).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this.

claim: Molecular graphics were performed with VMD and Chimera.
source: Molecular graphics were performed with VMD (Humphrey et al., 1996) and Chimera (Pettersen et al., 2004).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this with citations.

claim: .gro files containing molecular structure were used for all visualizations.
source: For all visualizations, .gro files containing molecular structure were used.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this.

claim: For two structures in Figure 3B, .xtc files were manually assigned to their corresponding coordinate files based on their names.
source: In the case of the two structures in Figure 3B, .xtc files were manually assigned to their corresponding .gro (for the TonB protein) or .tpr (for the T4 Lysozyme) files based on their names in their datasets.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this procedure.
